## kb_to_source

- Every normative prose claim on the reopened-setting and in-person surfaces traces to the source rule, factor, overwrite, base clause, lifecycle or tool docstring. Clarifications are entailments ("every exhibit recorded as received from the appellant ... whether it met the exhibit deadline or was recorded as late" <- "stand received"; "employer | yes | none on file -> reschedule window" <- neither tier condition; "Requests of every party on the appeal count alike" <- "subpoena requests on the appeal").
- "Before a reopened hearing on an employer's appeal the tax unit certifies the employer's account to the hearing officer ..." is the source rule's own sentence. It is not added procedure.
- No added confirmation/review/notification step. Worked examples recomputed (reopened 8/7/16; in-person 23/26/19; weekday tables) and are consistent.
- Prerequisite-side specific checks: cross-problem operational guidance — none; a task's opening world state written as policy fact — none (no doc states a dismissed rate appeal, Vietnamese request, a deficit-reserve account at rate 0.06, etc. as fact; all examples hypothetical).
- Minor visible-surface observation (not RED): the KB anchors the reopening window on "the mailing date of the dismissal, as shown on the Department's record of the appeal". The record field is `decision_mailed_date`, and nowhere does the KB say that this field holds the dismissal's mailing date for a dismissed appeal (the source's event-field meaning "decision_mailed_date: Date the dismissal was mailed" is not rendered). The `find_appeals` schema and the absence of any other mailing date make the reading unique, and the number is unaffected.
